record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling. The appendix Table 6 is labeled ToolLLaMA and repeats Table 5's values; the text separately says additional results include Gorilla, but the duplicated table does not identify a different model.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning methods suppress tool-use performance while retaining general-task performance. This conceptually tests unlearning effectiveness, but it uses a tool-unlearning task and does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the reported forget-tool performance (Tf) and average general-capability performance (TG) for the 20%-deletion comparisons in Tables 1 and 5. The study's LiRA-Tool results concern membership inference, not recovery of tool-use ability, so they are not rows for the listed recovery versions. Sequential-unlearning and ablation results are not included because they do not add a separate result for the claim's specified recovery attacks.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes ToolDelete for tool unlearning and reports forget-tool, retain-tool and general-task scores against adapted baselines. It runs no fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization or prompting recovery attack. LiRA-Tool is a membership-inference detector, not a recovery test. The paper itself lists adversarial evaluation as a limitation. The rows compare the study's own method with others, so they bear on no version of the shallow-unlearning claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude ToolDelete unlearns targeted tools while retaining other tools and general ability. They report it beats existing unlearning methods (12.5 and 9.1 accuracy points on forget and retain tools) and that it is efficient, sequential and works without training data. They list evaluation under adversarial conditions as a limitation and as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study formulates tool unlearning and evaluates tool-use task performance, rather than testing the listed recovery attacks after existing unlearning methods. It adapts several existing unlearning methods as baselines and proposes ToolDelete.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported forget-tool and general-capability outcomes vary by unlearning method and tool-augmented model/dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 11 adapted unlearning methods on two 7B tool-augmented LLMs, forget-tool success falls from about 76 to 29-58 with varying general-capability loss. No recovery attack is run.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-level unlearning methods differ in how well they remove tool-use skills while retaining other tools and general ability (pre-attack efficacy only).

fits_no_version.finding: LiRA-Tool TPR at FPR 0.01 is 0.14 for ToolDelete-DPO versus 0.18-0.21 for GradAscent and ICUL. This is detectability of tool presence, not recovery of the tool-use behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership-inference detectability of unlearned tools varies by method.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The paper does not specify a chance-level reference for forget-tool performance, and does not run the recovery attacks in the claim. Its stated limitations include evaluation under broader adversarial conditions and testing model scales beyond the 7B experiments. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated values.
record.rows_left_out: Tool unlearning test-set performance (TT), retained-tool performance (Tr), and individual general-capability task scores are omitted because the selected rows record the reported forget-tool metric and general-capability average bearing most directly on version A. Table 6 is omitted because it repeats Table 5's values while also being labeled ToolLLaMA; the text does not establish a distinct model for that duplicated table. LiRA-Tool membership-inference results are omitted because they measure detection of tool presence, not recovery of tool-use behavior.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover forgotten tool use; no chance-level reference is given. Only forget/retain scores of methods are reported.
No activation ablation, and no analysis of blocking access versus deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery attack. LiRA-Tool shadow prompts probe membership, not recovery.
ToolDelete is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks; adversarial robustness is left to future work.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are all method-comparison scores, including the study's own method, with no recovery test, so they are relinked to none. Table 6 duplicates Table 5 under the ToolLLaMA label, so the Gorilla results the text mentions are not actually shown. This does not bear on any version. The prompt-level blocking argument (ICUL) concerns an unlearning baseline, not a recovery attack.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests forget-tool performance and general-task retention, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks fail. It does not state a chance-level reference for Tf.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning attack to recover the forgotten tools is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of recovery by blocking access versus deleting knowledge is tested.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights is tested.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
ToolDelete is proposed as a tool-unlearning method, but the study does not test its resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

reader_labels.condition: ToolDelete-SFT and ToolDelete-DPO on ToolAlpaca and ToolLLaMA, deleting 20% of tools
reader_labels.reason: Both methods reduce forget-tool scores and retain general-capability averages relatively close to the original references, but the study reports no chance level and does not test recovery attacks (T1-ToolDeleteSFT-Tf, T1-ToolDeleteSFT-TG, T1-ToolDeleteDPO-Tf, T1-ToolDeleteDPO-TG, T5-ToolDeleteSFT-Tf, T5-ToolDeleteSFT-TG, T5-ToolDeleteDPO-Tf, T5-ToolDeleteDPO-TG).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Compared unlearning methods on ToolAlpaca and ToolLLaMA, deleting 20% of tools
reader_labels.reason: Forget-tool scores fall to varying degrees, while some methods also show reduced general-capability averages; none of these comparisons establishes chance-level performance (T1-GA-Tf, T1-GA-TG, T1-ICUL-Tf, T1-ICUL-TG, T5-GA-Tf, T5-GA-TG, T5-ICUL-Tf, T5-ICUL-TG).
